subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: Irritable bowel syndrome and chronic constipation

steps.tx: **Rome IV criteria** define irritable bowel syndrome as **recurrent abdominal pain**, on average at least **1** day a week in the last **3** months, with at least **2** of these links: pain related to defecation, a change in stool frequency, or a change in stool form. The criteria are version **4**. Symptoms should have started at least 6 months earlier. Alarm features such as bleeding, anaemia, or onset in later life are not part of IBS. The drawing shows the gut-brain loop that underlies the pain.
steps.say: Rome IV criteria require recurrent abdominal pain at least 1 day a week for the last 3 months, plus at least 2 of defecation, frequency or form. That is version 4, and symptoms began at least 6 months earlier. Bleeding or anaemia is not IBS.

vis.alt: Brain and bowel linked by nerves, with visceral hypersensitivity and altered motility.
vis.caption: Gut-brain signalling in irritable bowel syndrome. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **Bristol Stool Form Scale** runs from **Type 1**, separate hard lumps, to **Type 7**, watery stool with no solid pieces. **IBS subtypes** follow the usual form: IBS-C is constipation, IBS-D is diarrhoea, IBS-M is mixed, and IBS-U is unclassified. Ask the patient to point at the picture, because the words hard and loose are unreliable. The subtype chooses the drug. A secretagogue is wrong for watery IBS-D.
steps.say: The Bristol Stool Form Scale runs from Type 1 hard lumps to Type 7 watery stool. IBS subtypes are IBS-C, IBS-D, IBS-M and IBS-U. Let the patient match a picture. The subtype decides the drug.

steps.tx: **Linaclotide** and plecanatide are **guanylate cyclase-C agonists**. They raise cyclic GMP inside the enterocyte, open the CFTR chloride channel, and pull fluid into the lumen. Transit speeds up. They are drugs for IBS-C, not for diarrhoea. Diarrhoea is the adverse effect that makes people stop. They also reduce visceral pain, which is why they suit IBS-C better than a plain laxative.
steps.say: Linaclotide and plecanatide are guanylate cyclase-C agonists for IBS-C. Cyclic GMP activates CFTR, fluid enters the lumen, and transit speeds up. Diarrhoea is the reason patients stop, and they also ease visceral pain.

right.title: Stool softener alone
points: Does not target the pain pathway.
Not the exam drug for IBS-C.

steps.tx: **Lubiprostone** is an oral bicyclic fatty acid that opens **type 2 chloride channels**, called ClC-2, on the apical membrane. Chloride and water enter the lumen. Electrolyte balance is not the thing it disturbs. It is used in constipation, including IBS-C in women in several licences. Nausea is common. It is not a guanylate cyclase-C agonist, and it is not a 5-HT4 drug.
steps.say: Lubiprostone activates type 2 chloride channels on the enterocyte, so chloride and water enter the lumen. Nausea is common. It is not linaclotide and it is not prucalopride.

steps.tx: **Prucalopride** is a selective **5-HT4 receptor agonist**. It triggers colonic high-amplitude propagating contractions and is used for chronic idiopathic constipation when laxatives have failed. The digits are 5 and 4 in the receptor name. Older non-selective serotonin drugs were withdrawn for cardiac reasons. Prucalopride was designed to avoid that. It does not treat diarrhoea-predominant IBS.
steps.say: Prucalopride is a selective 5-HT4 receptor agonist. It starts high-amplitude colonic contractions and treats chronic idiopathic constipation after laxatives fail. It is not a drug for IBS-D. Older dirty serotonin drugs had cardiac problems. This one was built to avoid them.

steps.tx: **Eluxadoline** is a mixed mu and kappa opioid agonist and a delta opioid antagonist, used for IBS-D. It is strictly contraindicated if the gallbladder has been removed, because of **sphincter of Oddi spasm** and pancreatitis. Do not prescribe it after a cholecystectomy. It is also a poor choice with heavy alcohol use or a prior pancreatitis. It is the opposite of linaclotide: it slows the loose bowel rather than wetting a hard one.
steps.say: Eluxadoline treats IBS-D. It is banned after cholecystectomy because of sphincter of Oddi spasm and pancreatitis. It is avoided with heavy alcohol use or previous pancreatitis. It is not a drug for constipation.

left.title: Eluxadoline
points: Sphincter of Oddi spasm if no gallbladder.

right.title: Linaclotide
points: Diarrhoea, not pancreatitis, is the stop reason.

steps.tx: **Dyssynergic defecation** is a pelvic floor that tightens when it should relax. Diagnose it with high-resolution anorectal manometry and a failed **balloon expulsion test**: the patient cannot expel a **50** mL water-filled balloon within **1** minute. The drawing shows the puborectalis staying tight. Biofeedback is the treatment that works. Another laxative does not retrain the muscle. Do not label this IBS-C and stop.
steps.say: Dyssynergic defecation is diagnosed by anorectal manometry and a failed balloon expulsion test. The patient cannot pass a 50 millilitre balloon within 1 minute. Biofeedback is the treatment that retrains the pelvic floor. More laxatives do not.

vis.alt: Puborectalis stays contracted so the anorectal angle stays closed and stool does not pass.
vis.caption: Dyssynergic defecation, also called anismus. StewardMD original.

steps.tx: A **Low-FODMAP diet** cuts **fermentable oligosaccharides**, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols. Less fermentation means less gas and less stretch, and symptom relief is reported in up to **70%** of IBS patients. It is a trial of several weeks, then foods are put back. It is not a lifelong ban, and it is not a substitute for looking when alarm features are present. A dietitian should supervise it so the diet does not become deficient.
steps.say: A Low-FODMAP diet is a restriction of fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols. Up to 70 percent of IBS patients improve. Reintroduce foods afterwards. It is a trial, not a permanent rule, and alarm symptoms still need investigation.

nodes.label: Low-FODMAP diet for a few weeks
Reintroduce foods one at a time
